pages.title: Focusmate Alternative: Open Source Body Doubling | {app}
pages.description: Looking for a Focusmate alternative? {app} offers 1:1 virtual coworking sessions, open source privacy, flexible time blocks, and a free weekly plan.
pages.h1: An Open-Source Alternative to Focusmate for 1:1 Coworking
pages.intro: If you rely on one-on-one accountability to sit down and finish grading papers, writing code, or clearing your inbox, Focusmate likely showed you the value of body doubling. {app} takes that same quiet partnership and rebuilds it on an open-source foundation. You schedule a session, meet an accountability partner on camera, state your goal, and work quietly. Whether you need three free sessions a week or private self-hosting for your team, {app} provides structured focus without vendor lock-in.

sections.heading: How One-on-One Sessions Keep You on Track
sections.body:
Starting an intimidating task is often the hardest part of remote work. On {app}, you book a 25, 50, or 75 minute slot starting on the hour or half hour. When the session begins, you and your partner spend two minutes unmuting to share what you plan to accomplish, such as drafting a grant proposal or debugging a database migration. After declaring your intention, you mute your microphone, keep your video on, and work in silence.

Seeing another person working diligently in their own workspace creates gentle social pressure that prevents tab switching and phone scrolling. At the end of the block, a chime signals check-in time. You tell each other whether you completed the task, made partial progress, or hit an unexpected obstacle. Video streams are never recorded, keeping your home environment private, and community safety tools let you report or block anyone instantly.

sections.heading: Comparing {app} and Focusmate in Practice
sections.body:
Both platforms use structured one-on-one video appointments to help people beat procrastination through mutual accountability. Focusmate established the modern format of pairing two people for timed work blocks, offering a free tier limited to a few sessions each week alongside an upgraded tier for frequent users. At the time of writing (November 2026), {app} provides an alternative built on open principles, offering three free sessions weekly and an upgraded Plus plan with unlimited bookings, favorite partners, and advanced matching filters.

Both offer 25, 50 and 75 minute sessions. The bigger differences are in how the software is built and who controls it. {app} also includes personal booking links for study partners, university or workplace groups, and an upcoming hosted group option for up to nine participants. Most importantly, {app} is published under the AGPL-3.0 license, allowing organizations and privacy-minded individuals to review the source code or host an independent instance.

sections.heading: Open Source Independence and Data Sovereignty
sections.body:
Many remote professionals and academic researchers handle proprietary source code, confidential student records, or sensitive patient notes that cannot be exposed to closed third-party systems. Because {app} is released under the AGPL-3.0 license, your engineering team can audit every line of networking code, verify encryption standards, and ensure no unauthorized analytics track your team's workflow.

Organizations can self-host their own private {app} server on internal infrastructure. This allows corporate departments, lab groups, and university faculties to run closed coworking circles where colleagues only pair with vetted peers from the same domain. For individual users on the public service, open source means long-term transparency. The community shapes development priorities, and your productivity routines will never be disrupted by unexpected paywalls on basic data export or forced migrations.

sections.heading: Choosing the Right Coworking Platform for Your Routine
sections.body:
Focusmate remains a solid choice for people who want an established community with a high volume of active members around the clock. If you work erratic hours, such as three in the morning in your local time zone, Focusmate's deep booking roster makes finding an immediate partner reliable and quick.

{app} is better suited for individuals and teams who value software freedom and want to run focus sessions inside their own community. If you want personal booking links to invite trusted peers, or company-specific focus groups, {app} provides those tools. It is also the natural choice for users who care about software ethics and want the option to inspect or host the software themselves. Both services share the same core benefit: turning solitary work hours into shared, productive momentum.

faq.q: How does body doubling help with ADHD and task initiation?
faq.a: Body doubling serves as a practical support technique, not a medical treatment, for adults with ADHD who struggle to initiate solitary tasks. Having a calm, visible partner creates gentle external structure that reduces dread and executive dysfunction. Declaring your specific intentions aloud transforms ambiguous goals into clear, manageable commitments.

faq.q: Is my video feed ever recorded or stored during sessions?
faq.a: No, video feeds on {app} are peer-to-peer streams and are never recorded or saved to any server. You must keep your webcam turned on so your partner knows you are present, but your microphone remains muted after the check-in. You also retain full control to report or block an incompatible partner in one click.

faq.q: What session lengths does {app} support compared to Focusmate?
faq.a: {app} lets you book 25, 50, and 75 minute sessions starting on the hour or half hour. While 25 and 50 minute blocks work well for emails or administrative chores, the 75 minute option is designed for deep work like software development, academic writing, or long study sessions.

faq.q: Can I use {app} for free?
faq.a: Yes. The free plan on {app} includes three sessions per week, which is ideal for trying out the platform or anchoring your most difficult weekly projects. If you need unlimited sessions, custom partner filters, and favorite partner lists, you can upgrade to the Plus plan.

faq.q: How do university and company focus groups work?
faq.a: {app} allows institutions and remote companies to create dedicated focus groups. Members can restrict their matching pool to verified colleagues, students, or lab mates. This keeps coworking sessions within a familiar community while still maintaining the accountability and structure of standard public sessions.

pages.h1: A Quiet, Focused Alternative to Flow Club
pages.intro: If you find group video rooms overwhelming or prefer quiet partnerships over facilitated events, Flow Club might not match your work style. Flow Club uses paid, host-led groups with background music to foster community productivity. {app} takes a calmer approach centered on direct one-on-one accountability. You choose a time, meet one dedicated partner, share your objective, and work silently. With three free weekly sessions and an open-source codebase, {app} provides straightforward focus without social fatigue.

sections.heading: Direct One-on-One Focus Versus Hosted Group Rooms
sections.body:
Large group calls often demand noticeable social energy. In a facilitated group session, participants listen to host introductions, review group chat updates, and adapt to communal music choices. While some workers flourish in that communal atmosphere, many independent professionals lose momentum during long introductory rounds.

{app} eliminates performance anxiety by pairing you with a single partner for a 25, 50, or 75 minute session. Check-in takes under two minutes: you say your intended task aloud, your partner shares theirs, and both microphones mute. There is no host to entertain, no background soundtrack competing with your thoughts, and no side discussions in a text feed. You focus entirely on deep work, whether you are drafting a legal brief, organizing financial receipts, or refactoring frontend code.

sections.heading: A Contrast in Philosophy and Structure
sections.body:
Flow Club organizes its service around host-facilitated group video rooms available through a paid membership model. Their sessions emphasize social cohesion, host personalities, and group camaraderie. In contrast, {app} is built as an open, accessible productivity tool that offers three free sessions every week alongside an optional Plus membership for power users needing unlimited bookings and matching filters.

Rather than requiring paid subscriptions for any participation, {app} keeps the barrier to entry low so students, contractors, and job hunters can access consistent structure. Furthermore, {app} is open source under the AGPL-3.0 license. Anyone can inspect how the matching algorithms function or deploy a private instance on their own hardware. For users seeking group dynamics, {app} will soon introduce small hosted rooms of up to nine people, maintaining quiet productivity without forced socialization.

sections.heading: Reducing Sensory Load for Neurodivergent Workers
sections.body:
Many individuals with ADHD or autism find body doubling valuable because another person's presence provides an external anchor against distractibility. However, body doubling is a supportive habit rather than a clinical treatment, and excessive sensory input can undermine its effectiveness. Facilitated group calls with changing speaker views, active chat boxes, and curated music playlists can quickly cause cognitive overload.

{app} reduces sensory stimulation to the bare essentials. Video is mandatory to ensure genuine accountability, but microphones stay muted during work blocks so you can listen to your own preferred ambient sounds or work in complete silence. You interact with only one partner at a time, lowering social anxiety. If you ever encounter an unhelpful match, you can block or report them with a single click, keeping your focus space predictable and secure.

sections.heading: Determining Which Coworking Environment Suits You
sections.body:
Deciding between these platforms depends on whether you seek social entertainment or solitary concentration during your workday. Flow Club is an appealing option if you thrive on high-energy group motivation, appreciate host-curated playlists, and enjoy active community banter during work breaks. If having a host guide the session helps you feel supported, their subscription service delivers that experience.

{app} is designed for workers who prefer quiet efficiency and direct responsibility. If you want to log in, state your goals to a single accountability partner, and get straight to work without waiting through group introductions, {app} fits your schedule better. It also accommodates budget-conscious freelancers who need a reliable free tier, as well as teams and universities that want to self-host custom focus groups within their own closed communities.

faq.q: Why does {app} prioritize one-on-one sessions over large groups?
faq.a: One-on-one sessions eliminate social performance and waiting times. When working with a single partner, you establish personal accountability in under two minutes without listening to dozen-person roll calls. It creates a calm, focused environment where both individuals remain mutually responsible for their committed goals.

faq.q: Does {app} play background music during sessions?
faq.a: No, {app} does not broadcast music or audio during work intervals. Microphones are muted so each participant can control their own auditory environment. You can listen to your own focus music, noise-canceling white noise, or work in total quiet without conflicting with anyone else.

faq.q: Can I join sessions without paying a subscription?
faq.a: Yes. {app} provides a free tier that gives you three sessions per week without requiring payment details. If your schedule demands daily multiple sessions, you can upgrade to the Plus plan for unlimited bookings, favorite partner lists, and advanced partner filters.

faq.q: How does {app} handle upcoming group sessions?
faq.a: While {app} is centered on pairs, small group sessions of up to nine people are coming soon. These sessions will maintain a low-distraction ethic, emphasizing quiet productivity and brief verbal check-ins rather than extensive social hosting or loud presentations.

faq.q: Is {app} suitable for private company teams?
faq.a: Yes. Because {app} is open source under the AGPL-3.0 license, companies can self-host internal servers where team members only pair with colleagues. Alternatively, organizations can set up private groups on the hosted platform to encourage cross-departmental focus sessions.

pages.intro: Caveday popularized the concept of guided focus blocks called caves, bringing participants together for facilitated sprints complete with group warm-ups and mindful check-ins. sections.heading: Fitting Focus Sessions Into a Busy Daily Routine
sections.body:
Committing to a scheduled multi-hour workshop requires clearing large segments of your afternoon, which is difficult for consultants, customer-facing professionals, and graduate students balancing lectures with lab work. Missing a pre-scheduled workshop start can derail an entire afternoon of intended deep work.

{app} is designed to integrate seamlessly into ordinary workdays. Sessions start every thirty minutes, both on the hour and half-hour, around the clock. You can book a swift 25-minute sprint between client consultations to clear urgent invoices, or reserve a 50-minute block to draft a research abstract. For intensive writing or coding tasks, 75-minute sessions provide extended immersion. Because sessions are self-directed between you and your partner, you never lose fifteen minutes to facilitator greetings or communal stretching routines.

sections.heading: Contrasting Facilitated Caves With Peer Accountability
sections.body:
Caveday structures its service around trained guides who lead group focus sprints known as caves. These events incorporate structured routines, guided breathing exercises, and communal chat reflections. This format appeals to participants who enjoy intentional structure and guided workshop atmospheres. However, accessing these events requires purchasing passes or memberships.

{app} approaches productivity from a decentralized, peer-driven perspective. Instead of relying on a trained guide, you pair directly with another working adult. Accountability arises from mutual presence and spoken commitment rather than external facilitation. {app} provides a free plan granting three sessions weekly, with an optional Plus tier offering unlimited bookings and custom filtering. Furthermore, {app} is fully open source under the AGPL-3.0 license, meaning teams can host their own private infrastructure rather than relying on a commercial provider.

sections.heading: Practical Peer Support for Executive Dysfunction
sections.body:
Procrastination often stems from emotional friction around complex or unstructured projects, such as preparing tax documents or outlining a dissertation chapter. Many people with ADHD describe body doubling as an effective support technique, though it should be recognized as a practical coping tool rather than medical treatment. The physical presence of a focused peer provides a grounding anchor that stabilizes attention.

In facilitated group calls, the social overhead of participating in icebreakers or guided exercises can inadvertently trigger performance anxiety. {app} removes that barrier by keeping interactions concise and transactional. You greet your partner, summarize your goal in plain words, and work quietly with cameras enabled. When the chime sounds at the conclusion, you report whether you finished, made partial progress, or stalled, closing the loop without judgment.

sections.heading: When to Pick Caveday and When to Choose {app}
sections.body:
Caveday is an excellent option for individuals seeking an immersive, guided workshop experience. If you enjoy having an enthusiastic facilitator guide your schedule, lead reflective mindfulness exercises, and manage group pacing during dedicated multi-hour retreats, Caveday delivers high-touch support that feels like an interactive classroom.

{app} is the better fit if you want streamlined, self-paced accountability that slips into narrow gaps in your calendar. If you prefer quiet one-on-one partnership over group activities, {app} lets you get to work immediately without guided rituals. It is also the right platform if you value open-source software, wish to keep your usage completely free for occasional needs, or want to create private focus circles for your company or university department.

faq.q: Does {app} include guided meditation or facilitator warm-ups?
faq.a: No, {app} does not incorporate guided meditation, breathwork, or facilitator introductions. Sessions are strictly peer-to-peer. You and your accountability partner exchange brief goal statements for two minutes and then work in silence. This design prioritizes immediate immersion in your personal tasks without additional social rituals.

faq.q: Can I book back-to-back sessions on {app}?
faq.a: Yes, you can schedule consecutive sessions to build your own extended work block. For example, you can book two 50-minute sessions with a ten-minute break between them, or combine a 75-minute deep sprint with a shorter 25-minute administrative review.

faq.q: Are sessions on {app} limited to specific hours of the day?
faq.a: No, {app} operates continuously across all time zones. Sessions begin on every hour and half-hour, twenty-four hours a day. Whether you work early mornings, standard office hours, or late night shifts, you can find a time slot that matches your routine.

faq.q: How does {app} ensure user accountability without hosts?
faq.a: Accountability relies on mutual visibility and explicit commitments. Having your webcam on with a live partner creates natural focus, while the requirement to report progress as done, partial, or not done at the end provides closure. You can also save favorite partners to work with trusted peers regularly.

faq.q: Is self-hosting {app} difficult for small teams?
faq.a: Deploying {app} on your own servers is straightforward because the project is licensed under the AGPL-3.0. Teams with basic sysadmin experience can spin up a self-hosted instance, ensuring that internal communications, scheduling records, and member directories remain entirely under your organization's administrative control.

sections.heading: Focusing on Action Rather Than Productivity Content
sections.body:
When dealing with challenging projects like data analysis or manuscript revisions, it is easy to fall into productive procrastination by reading articles, adjusting dashboard settings, or sampling ambient music tracks. {app} eliminates peripheral features in favor of pure execution. The interface is intentionally minimalist: you view your calendar, select a time slot, and enter a quiet video room with an accountability partner. There are no discussion boards to monitor, no meditation tracks to configure, and no wellness webinars to attend. You bring your own work and your preferred tools. By keeping the interface completely uncluttered, {app} ensures that logging onto the platform leads directly to deep concentration rather than passive consumption.

Flown organizes its service around scheduled group sessions known as flocks, guided by facilitators who introduce session themes and maintain group momentum. {app} departs from this model by emphasizing quiet peer partnership over group facilitation. sections.heading: Low-Pressure Body Doubling for Solitary Work
sections.body:
Working remotely can feel isolating, and open-ended deadlines often paralyze motivation. Many people with ADHD describe body doubling as an effective support technique that bridges the gap between planning a task and actually executing it, though it functions as a practical behavioral support rather than a medical treatment. Simply knowing someone is working alongside you reduces the urge to seek immediate digital distractions.

In large guided calls, participants can easily blend into the background with cameras turned off, diminishing accountability. On {app}, cameras are required, while microphones remain muted throughout the session. Because you are working one-on-one, your mutual presence creates genuine commitment. Flown is a strong option for professionals who appreciate a comprehensive lifestyle and focus platform. faq.q: Why is {app} released as open-source software?
